intro.h2: The people who draw it are the people who build it
paragraphs: Transitions has handled kitchen remodeling in Norwell, MA and across the South Shore since 2006. Many firms call themselves design-build and then hand the job to subcontractors. Here, design, material selection, project management, demolition, carpentry and installation are all done by Transitions employees.

The licensed trades, plumbing, electrical and tile, come from the same crews on every job, and they have worked with the firm for years. Craig Ricciarelli, the founder, still estimates each remodel himself before the contract. Because one team owns the design and the build, the full scope is priced up front and change orders are rare and the budget holds.

services.h2: Four ways to work with Transitions

items.name: Kitchen Remodeling
items.blurb: Floor plans, elevations and 3D renderings, then demolition, framing, plumbing, electrical, tile, cabinets and finish carpentry by the in-house team. A dedicated project manager handles permits and inspections, with daily cleanup and dust containment. The team has completed more than 800 kitchens.

image.alt: Two-tone Milton, MA kitchen with an Indigo navy Mouser island, white Divinity perimeter cabinets and brass hardware

items.name: Bathroom Remodeling
items.blurb: Primary baths, hall and family baths, powder rooms and new bathroom additions. The team redesigns from the studs out or refreshes the existing footprint, covering layout, shower and tub design, vanities, tile and stone, plumbing fixtures, lighting and mirrors. More than 400 bathrooms are complete.

image.alt: Braintree, MA primary bath with a rift sawn white oak floating vanity, Arctic White quartz and LED mirrors

items.name: First Floor Remodels
items.blurb: For homes remodeled piece by piece over the years, the whole main level is designed as one: kitchen, baths, mudroom, pantry and laundry, with bump-outs where needed. One designer and project manager stay with you from the first sketch to the final walkthrough.

image.alt: Marshfield, MA first floor remodel with a white quartz island, leather counter stools, white oak pantry cabinets and a linear pendant

items.name: Custom Cabinetry, Supplied or Installed
items.blurb: Working with your own contractor? Transitions can design your kitchen and deliver the cabinetry, countertops and hardware, or supply and install them. Lines include Mouser, Tedd Wood and Diamond. Local builders use the same service through the firm's Builder Partnership Program.

image.alt: Builder partnership kitchen in Norwell, MA with walnut base cabinets, glass-front gray uppers and white subway tile

about.text: Craig Ricciarelli has run his own businesses for nearly 40 years. He founded Transitions in 2006 and still oversees every project that comes through the door. Linda Ricciarelli handles accounting, payroll and job costing, and Nick Ricciarelli came back to the family business from a career in tech to run operations. Designers John Donahue, a Braintree native designing kitchens since 1999, Karen King, with the firm since 2008, and Scituate native Veronica Dee Amelang guide selections, while project manager PJ Mottola runs the build. Clients return for second projects and refer friends.

image.alt: Craig Ricciarelli, founder of Transitions Kitchens, Baths and Remodeling in Norwell, MA

process.h2: Free through design, then one team builds it

steps.title: Showroom visit
steps.text: Tour 5,000 square feet of displays, meet your designer and compare cabinets, counters, tile and fixtures side by side. The visit is free.

steps.title: In-home measure
steps.text: Your designer measures your space, confirms the scope and photographs site conditions. This step is also free.

steps.title: Design and budget appointment
steps.text: See initial concepts and a preliminary budget. A design agreement with a 5% deposit then secures your full design package.

steps.title: Final design and line-item budget
steps.text: The construction team reviews the design in your home, then you get a line-item budget and timeline before signing the contract.

steps.title: Build and walkthrough
steps.text: Permits, demolition, framing, plumbing, electrical, cabinets, counters and trim follow in order, ending with a final punch list walkthrough.

service_area.h2: From Hingham to Plymouth and west to Wellesley
service_area.text: Transitions is based on Washington Street in Norwell and works with homeowners across the South Shore and Greater Boston. Crews are regularly in Hingham, Cohasset, Scituate, Marshfield, Duxbury, Hanover and Plymouth, and inland in Milton, Canton, Needham, Wellesley and Newton. Materials-only orders have gone as far as Martha's Vineyard. Not sure about your town? Call, because the team would rather talk about fit than turn you away by zip code.

faq.h2: Before you plan a South Shore remodel

items.q: Is the first showroom visit really free?
items.a: Yes. Your first showroom visit and conversation cost nothing and carry no obligation, and the in-home measure and first design and budget meeting are free too. You pay a 5% design deposit only when you sign the design agreement, so you see a full estimate before any real commitment.

items.q: How far ahead should I start planning a kitchen?
items.a: Transitions recommends reaching out 2 to 3 months before your ideal start date. Design, material selection and ordering all take time, and cabinets and other materials can have long lead times. Starting early makes for a smoother schedule once construction begins.

items.q: Do I need an appointment to visit the Norwell showroom?
items.a: No. Walk-ins are welcome Monday to Friday 9:00 am to 5:00 pm and Saturday 9:00 am to 3:00 pm. Booking ahead just makes sure a designer is free to give you full attention. After you send the online form, you can pick a showroom time right away.

items.q: Can I buy cabinets only and use my own contractor?
items.a: Yes. With the materials-only service, Transitions designs the kitchen, selects and orders cabinetry, countertops and hardware, inspects them and delivers to your home. You or your contractor install. A materials-and-installation option adds installation by the Transitions team without the full remodel.

items.q: Do you build additions with a kitchen or bath?
items.a: Smaller additions and bump-outs, yes, especially when they support a kitchen or bath layout already being remodeled. A Marshfield family moved its pantry and laundry into a new rear addition to bring light into the kitchen. Larger additions are taken case by case, usually as part of a bigger remodel.

final_cta.text: Call (781) 871-0881 or stop by 433 Washington St in Norwell, and meet a designer the same day.
